extra_misconceptions.fact: Isolated trees attract lightning strikes; golfers must move to an enclosed building or lightning shelter and drop their metal clubs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing under a tall tree on the fairway provides safe protection from lightning until the rain passes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Puncturing an intact blister invites bacterial infection; cover the hot spot or blister with moleskin or a sterile adhesive bandage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Popping a friction blister on your hand or heel with a tee lets you keep swinging without discomfort.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hot water opens pores and spreads urushiol oil; rinse exposed skin immediately with cool water and mild soap or rubbing alcohol.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scrubbing skin with hot water and harsh soap hours after retrieving a ball from poison ivy prevents a rash.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Continuing to bear weight worsens ligament damage; stop playing and apply rest, ice, compression, and elevation right away.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Walking off a freshly sprained ankle across the remaining holes keeps the joint loose and speeds up recovery.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a golfer seek shelter immediately when lightning strikes on an open fairway far from the clubhouse?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lifting the center tears grass roots and kills the turf; push grass inward from the outer edges and tap the surface flat with a putter.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prying up the center of a pitch mark on the putting green with a tee is the proper way to level the turf.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The USGA Rules of Golf limit a ball search to three minutes from when the player or their caddie begins looking for it.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Golfers have five full minutes under the current USGA Rules of Golf to search for a ball in the rough before it is lost.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Total strokes plus penalties equals the gross score, whereas the net score subtracts the player's handicap strokes from the gross score.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A golfer's net score on a hole is the total number of strokes taken plus any penalty strokes before applying a handicap.

extra_misconceptions.fact: USGA Rules allow amateurs to accept non-cash prizes and even cash up to the current thousand-dollar limit in scratch competitions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Amateur golfers cannot accept any retail merchandise prize or trophy in a tournament without losing their amateur status.
